s.note: Cabbie has been driving that island for years and never stops to eat.
s.how: Freeze 600g topside for 1 hour, then slice 3mm thick across the grain. Mix 80ml soy sauce, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp garlic powder. Marinate the beef overnight. Pat dry, lay on racks over trays and dry at 75C with the oven door slightly open for 3 to 4 hours until leathery but still bendy.

s.note: Sardines straight from the can, in a city with no shops.
s.how: Drain 2 tins sardines in oil, about 220g. Lay a sardine on each of 24 saltine crackers, squeeze over lemon, add a drop of hot sauce and a little chopped parsley. Serve on the tin lids for the full survival look.

m.note: Smoky sausage, potato and bean stew, whatever the Duke's crew could find on the island.
m.how: Brown 500g sliced smoked sausage in a big pot. Add 1 diced onion, 2 carrots and 600g diced potatoes, cook 5 minutes, then 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 can cannellini beans, 400g crushed tomatoes and 750ml chicken stock. Simmer 30 minutes, add a quarter cabbage shredded for the last 10, season and serve in mugs.

w.note: Chocolate oat slice, the kind you'd stash in your pocket on Manhattan prison island.
w.how: Melt 150g butter with 3 tbsp golden syrup and 100g brown sugar. Stir in 250g rolled oats and a pinch of salt, then press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin. Bake at 180C for 20 minutes until golden. Melt 150g dark chocolate, spread over the warm slice and sprinkle with flaky salt. Cool, chill for 1 hour and cut into 16 bars.

d.note: Fresh lemon and sugar shaken with ice and soda, in jam jars, for the bridge run.
d.how: Shake the juice of 4 lemons and 80ml sugar syrup with ice. Strain into 4 ice-filled jam jars and top with 600ml soda water.
